answer: A harbor registry can resist sybils by tying each agent identity to a verifiable stake and a history of useful work, rather than to a free account. Like a vine that only grows where it is tended, reputation should accumulate slowly through attested tasks and decay when idle, so creating thousands of fresh identities gains nothing. Each new claim must echo prior verified work, with signed receipts from independent peers, before it earns spending power, making mass fake identities expensive and easy to spot.
